::: {.cite-bar .domain-intelligence}
[Lapsed]{.status .status-lapsed} [Pub. L. 118-49]{.cite} [138 Stat. 862]{.cite}
:::

Reauthorized Section 702 for two years, the shortest extension to date, and made the most extensive changes to FISA since 2008, concentrated on how the FBI may search collected data for information about Americans.

## Key provisions

- Extended Title VII of FISA to April 2026.
- Tightened FBI query rules: fewer authorized personnel, supervisor or attorney approval, and a ban on queries meant only to find evidence of a crime.
- Broadened the definition of electronic communication service provider, the most contested change.
- Barred any restart of 'abouts' collection and added counternarcotics to the definition of foreign intelligence.

## Why it matters

A warrant requirement for U.S. person queries failed in the House on a tie vote, which set the terms of the 2026 fight. It amends [FISA](fisa-1978.qmd) and reauthorized [the FISA Amendments Act](fisa-amendments-2008.qmd).

## Current status

Its two-year reauthorization of Section 702 ran to April 20, 2026. Congress passed a 10-day and then a 45-day extension, and the authority lapsed in mid-June 2026. Check current status before relying on this page.
